subject.title: fix(cli): reject oversized --file input before reading in config patch

question: Should `config patch` adopt a documented input-size limit, and must that limit apply identically to `--file` and `--stdin`?
rationale: Current behavior and public docs do not establish the proposed 1 MiB limit, so choosing the permanent cap and compatibility policy is a product/API decision rather than a mechanical bug fix.

options.title: Define one shared cap
options.body: Choose and document a config-patch byte limit, then enforce it consistently for file and stdin input with pre-read optimization and a final cap check.

options.title: Keep inputs uncapped
options.body: Do not add the arbitrary 1 MiB rejection; address resource usage only through an existing generic bounded-input contract if one is adopted later.

options.title: Accept file-only limit
options.body: Intentionally allow file and stdin modes to differ, with explicit documentation and upgrade guidance for affected scripts.

recommendation.title: Define one shared cap
recommendation.body: Choose and document a config-patch byte limit, then enforce it consistently for file and stdin input with pre-read optimization and a final cap check.

likelyOwner.reason: The recent config CLI refactor and public CLI-reference history make this the strongest available owner for deciding the command contract.
